# Game timer from ASSS 1.4.4 src/core/game_timer.c (compiled unmodified).
# A replayable transcript. '# <label>:' starts a scenario and zeroes the arena's
# timerdata; the harness drives the clock, so every tick value here is exact.
#   at <ticks>           set current_ticks() to this (1 tick = 10 ms)
#   create / confchanged / destroy   ran ArenaAction(AA_CREATE/AA_CONFCHANGED/AA_DESTROY)
#   tick                 ran TimerMaster(), which ASSS's mainloop calls every 100 ticks
#   timer <args> / time / timereset / pausetimer   ran that ?command for the player
#   state <enabled> <gamelen> <timeout>   the module's timerdata afterwards
#   chat <player|arena> <sound|-> <text>  every line the module emitted since the
#                        previous state line, in order; '-' means no sound code.
# Rules these records pin:
#   Misc:TimedGame is in TICKS, not seconds, and a non-zero value arms the timer at
#     AA_CREATE. AA_CONFCHANGED arms it only when the OLD value was zero and the new
#     one is not -- raising 3000 to 6000 leaves the running timeout alone.
#   TimerMaster fires when TICK_GT(now, timeout), i.e. strictly past; landing exactly
#     on the timeout is not yet expired. On expiry a TimedGame arena re-arms to
#     now+gamelen and keeps going; a ?timer-created one (gamelen 0) disables itself
#     and zeroes timeout.
#   Warnings come from Misc:TimerWarnings, split on spaces and commas, at most 5
#     values kept (strsplit is only called while i < 5, so a 6th is never read).
#     A warning fires only on the tick where (timeout - now)/100 EQUALS the value,
#     so a tick that steps over it is silently missed. A value that is a multiple of
#     60 is announced in minutes, with 60 itself as the only singular 'minute'.
#   ?timer only works when TimedGame is 0, and parses '<mins>[:<secs>]' with strtol,
#     so trailing junk is ignored but a non-numeric start is rejected. It replies by
#     calling ?time, which is why those records carry two chat lines.
#   ?pausetimer subtracts current_ticks() from timeout to park a remaining duration
#     there, and adds it back on resume -- while paused, 'timeout' is a DURATION, and
#     ?time reports it with the 'paused at' wording. It does nothing in a TimedGame
#     arena. ?timereset only works in one.
# TimedGame 0, arena create does not arm: TimedGame 0 TimerWarnings [] t0 1000
create
state 0 0 0
tick
state 0 0 0
time
state 0 0 0
chat player - Time left: 0 minutes 0 seconds
# ?timer in a non-TimedGame arena: TimedGame 0 TimerWarnings [] t0 1000
create
state 0 0 0
timer 5
state 1 0 31000
chat player - Time left: 5 minutes 0 seconds
at 1500
time
state 1 0 31000
chat player - Time left: 4 minutes 55 seconds
timer 2:30
state 1 0 16500
chat player - Time left: 2 minutes 30 seconds
timer 0:7
state 1 0 2200
chat player - Time left: 0 minutes 7 seconds
timer abc
state 1 0 2200
chat player - timer format is: '?timer mins[:secs]'
timer 1junk
state 1 0 7500
chat player - Time left: 1 minutes 0 seconds
timereset
state 1 0 7500
